title: Customer signal fixpack and priority extract
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact working extract for a small 'fixpack' we can attempt in Q1 to address high-frequency, low-effort customer friction across inference runtime and API ergonomics. Goal: surface 6–8 actionable items, annotate with rough impact/effort, and propose next-step owners.

Topline synthesis (3 lines):
- Customers keep hitting predictable runtime edge cases (small inputs + long context combos) that amplify token cost and cause KV-cache thrashing.
- Several asks are ergonomics-driven: clearer error contexts, better sampling behavior docs, and an opt-in aggressive prefix-caching toggle.
- There are low-effort mitigations (config knobs, SDK helpers, telemetry flags) that give near-term relief while platform-level batching/cache tuning proceeds.

Signal cuts (counts from CS ticket scrape, Nov–Dec 2025):
- Runtime cache churn / token blowups: ~27 tickets (tier: mid-to-high impact)
- Unexpected 413/timeout during streaming at short prompt lengths: ~11 tickets
- Confusing SDK errors + missing actionable meter: ~19 tickets
- Cost-surprise from repeated short completions (no prefix reuse): ~22 tickets

Representative quotes (anonymized):
- "We keep seeing token invoices jump when we changed to longer context; nothing in the logs explains the spike."
- "Streaming fails sometimes with no error message — client just receives an empty connection close."
- "If there was a simple boolean to say 'favor-cost' vs 'favor-latency' that would help ops teams a lot."

Candidate fixes (ranked quick → medium):
1) Quick: SDK helper: "smart_prefix_cache" (opt-in flag) — when enabled, SDK attaches a stable prefix-id that seeds KV-cache reuse for repeated short completions.
   - Why: Many customers repeat similar short calls where cache warmup causes cost/latency.
   - Rough effort: 1 dev + 1 QA for 1 sprint to prototype; server change: small header handling and cache-keying tweak.
   - Expected impact: high (reduces token duplication for repeat calls).
   - Suggested owner: devexp (Avery) + serving-runtime eng (Samir).

2) Quick: Improve streaming error surface — return structured error code + guidance text when connection closes prematurely.
   - Effort: ~3 days (runtime + SDK).
   - Impact: medium-high (reduces customer confusion and support load).
   - Owner: sre + devexp.

3) Quick: Billing preview telemetry flag (trial mode) — allow customer to see token-estimates per route in Console for 48h.
   - Effort: 2 weeks (console + analytics hooks).
   - Impact: medium (addresses cost-surprise).
   - Owner: product-console (Maya).

4) Medium: Batching policy presets (console + API) — Low-latency, Balanced, Cost-optimized presets that map to batching/cold-start thresholds and cache TTLs.
   - Effort: 2 sprints (analysis + UI + runtime knobs).
   - Impact: high (gives teams clear trade-off knobs).
   - Owner: product-hosted-api + serving-runtime.

5) Medium: Canary a new cache-key strategy for mixed-length sequences (experimental backend) — track cold-start ratio and token delta per route; rollback if QoS degrades.
   - Effort: cross-team spike (3–4 weeks).
   - Impact: high if safe.
   - Owner: applied-ml + serving-runtime.

6) Investigate: Silent 413s during streaming under NGINX front-proxy (customer infra patterns) — many reports point to client side keepalive + proxy timeouts.
   - Action: replicate with traffic replay and capture wire traces.
   - Owner: sre + solutions-eng.

Low-friction UX clarifications (<=1 week copy/dev):
- Add "what to check" checklist for unexpected cost spikes (include KV hit-rate, repeated prompt patterns, model/quantization).
- Add clear sampling/temp/seed docs for SDK that explain nondeterministic outputs and reproducibility steps.

Prioritization rationale:
- Quick wins that require mostly flags or small SDK additions are first because they materially reduce CS triage load and customer pain.
- Console/batching presets are a medium-term product bet that reduce future pressure on runtime optimizations.

Metrics to measure success (initial):
- 30-day change in ticket volume for the three signal cuts above.
- Token cost variance per customer (pre/post) — aim to reduce 95th percentile surprises.
- Time-to-first-response for streaming errors (internal) and reduction in support escalation.

Open questions / unknowns (to resolve before rollout):
- Will prefix-anchoring create correctness problems for stateful chat flows? Need short safety test matrix.
- Do customers want the "favor-cost" knob exposed in API or only Console? (ask field leads)
- What telemetry quota/retention is needed to compute per-route cold-start deltas cheaply?

Suggested next steps (week-by-week starter plan):
- Week 0: Align owners + create minimal tickets (Avery to raise feature tickets and link RD-5123 as a parent).
- Week 1: Ship streaming error surface change + SDK patch (alpha) and add Console checklist text.
- Week 2–3: Prototype smart_prefix_cache as behind-flag in SDK + runtime. Run internal canary against reproducible customer traffic.
- Week 4–8: Decide on batching presets scope; run spike and gather telemetry.

Risks / mitigation: 
- Risk: Prefix anchoring could exacerbate stale state for chat — mitigation: only enable for stateless short completions and add user-visible header to opt-in gradually.
- Risk: Telemetry cost for per-route analysis — mitigation: sample 1% and progressively increase for routes that show high variance.

Notes & backchannel:
- Slack thread: #cs-runtime-pain (see pinned messages for sample traces).
- Related GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/312 (streaming error codes).
- Parent signal registry: Confluence link in linked_artifacts.

Quick reference: decision owners and tentative dates:
- Streaming errors (ship alpha): Samir — target 2026-01-15
- SDK smart_prefix_cache (alpha behind flag): Avery — target 2026-02-05
- Billing preview telemetry (console): Maya — target 2026-02-12

Appendix (raw tickest snippets):
- TKT-9382: "Sudden token bill spike after switch to context 32k — logs show repeated prefix tokens."
- TKT-9459: "Streaming closed by server, no body, no code — our client has to reconnect 3x."
- TKT-9520: "We need more knobs for balancing cost vs latency. Our SRE wants an API toggle to enforce batching."

End of extract. This is intentionally compact — use this as the working scaffold for a small fixpack PR and link to ticket RD-5123 as the orchestration epic.
